rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the eight-compound elution window and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A 10-minute gradient at intermediate temperature provides a baseline for subsequent slope and temperature comparisons.

Keep the gradient unchanged and raise temperature to test selectivity of the sole critical pair, currently at R = 0.72. Higher temperature should also preserve the favorable last-peak time below 10 minutes.

Make the gradient one step shallower at the favorable temperature to raise the critical pair from R = 1.41 toward full resolution. The current last-peak time of 6.56 minutes leaves ample room to gain resolution without incurring a time penalty.

The maximum CRF is already achieved; now test a shorter fully resolved method while retaining injection 3 as the benchmark. This gradient slope lies between injections 2 and 3, so it should preserve R above 1.5 for the critical pair while shortening the last-peak time.

Test a trimmed gradient window to shorten the fully resolved separation, retaining injection 4 as the benchmark. The slightly shallower slope may protect the critical early pair while the higher starting organic fraction reduces retention.

Restore the lower starting organic fraction to protect the critical early pair, using a slope only slightly steeper than the fully resolved injection 4. This should trim the last-peak time while keeping all eight peaks within the gradient and targeting CRF 1.000.

With maximum CRF secured, test whether lower-temperature selectivity permits a steeper, faster fully resolved gradient. The critical pair may separate more strongly on the low-temperature side of an elution-order crossover; the broad gradient should still elute all compounds well before 42 minutes.

Raise temperature one step from injection 7 to split the late three-peak cluster while testing whether the early pair retains full resolution. Keeping the gradient fixed isolates the temperature response in this potentially useful low-temperature selectivity region.

Return to the successful high-temperature region and test a slope just steeper than injection 6, targeting the shortest fully resolved separation. The last peak should elute shortly into the final hold, while the critical early pair is expected to remain near R = 1.5.

Reduce the endpoint one grid step from injection 5 to test whether a shallower trimmed gradient restores full resolution of its R = 1.44 early pair. This probes an alternative maximum-score method with a higher starting organic fraction, while retaining injection 9 as the fastest fully resolved benchmark.

With maximum CRF secured, test a higher starting organic fraction in the lower-temperature selectivity region for a potentially faster alternative. Moving to 35 C should spread the late cluster seen at 30 C, while the changed gradient window tests whether the early pair can remain resolved.

Lengthen injection 11’s gradient to determine whether its critical early pair responds sufficiently to slope at 35 C. This should improve resolution while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes, testing a fully resolved alternative at a lower temperature.

Test a slightly steeper gradient than injection 9 to locate the fastest full-resolution boundary at 60 C. The critical pair will likely be very close to R = 1.5, while the higher endpoint avoids any final-hold delay for the last peak.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction changes selectivity enough to resolve the late cluster at 30 C while preserving the favorable early-pair separation. This explores a potentially faster alternative; injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Lower the starting organic fraction from injection 12 to improve its nearly resolved early pair while retaining adequate separation of the later peaks. This tests a lower-temperature maximum-score alternative, with the last peak expected to remain below 10 minutes.

Refine the higher-starting-organic branch with a slope between injections 5 and 10, targeting full resolution with less retention than injection 10. Injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Test the next slightly steeper grid-accessible slope above injection 16 to approach the full-resolution boundary for phi0 = 0.10. The early pair should remain close to R = 1.5, with a modest reduction in last-peak time.

Test a further increase in starting organic fraction with a compensating shallower gradient to preserve early-pair resolution. This maps whether a more tightly trimmed window can provide another maximum-score method; injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved separation.

Preserve injection 3’s successful gradient slope and temperature while trimming the endpoint and programmed gradient duration. All peaks should elute before the gradient ends, retaining CRF 1.000 with more resolution margin than the faster injection 9.

With CRF already maximized, test a shallower gradient for greater resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. This should strengthen the early critical pair, though the narrowing gap between peaks 3 and 4 needs monitoring.

Test a trimmed version of injection 20 to bring the last peak forward while retaining more resolution margin than the fastest methods. The shallower slope should compensate for the higher starting organic fraction, with all peaks expected before 10 minutes.

Steepen injection 20 slightly to shorten retention while preserving a useful resolution margin for both early critical pairs. This should retain the maximum CRF and provide an intermediate option between the fastest separation and the more conservatively resolved method.

Shorten injection 22’s separation by raising the endpoint one grid step while retaining the favorable starting composition and temperature. The critical early pair should remain comfortably above R = 1.5, preserving maximum CRF with less retention time.

Steepen injection 21’s gradient to shorten retention while preserving more early-pair resolution margin than injection 16. This targets another maximum-score method near the established resolution boundary; injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Use the final injection on a maximum-score candidate with the same successful slope as injection 3 but a shorter programmed gradient. It should retain R near 1.67 and a last-peak time near 7.49 minutes; injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.
